title: Encoded adjacency word
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $s,n$ be natural numbers. Form the Boolean word of length $n^2$ whose entry at each index $k<n^2$ is true exactly when there is an edge at input $x$ and parameter $s$ from vertex $\lfloor k/n\rfloor$ to vertex $k\bmod n$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet
caveat: The formal definition uses division and remainder by $n$, including when $n=0$; the prose's quotient and remainder notation is understood in the natural-number convention.
